transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for having me. Um, I hope I'm not taking up time someone else might need more. 

It's just... well, I came in because I've been getting really stuck on this... this sagging, uneven spot right around my jaw and my neck. I know I probably shouldn't let it bother me so much, and I try not to be vain about it, but I just can't stop seeing it. Folks tell me it looks normal, but... well, I just feel like it’s the very first thing the families I work with, or the nurses, or even just the people at my church notice when they look at me. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds a bit silly, to be so worried about how I look. Is it okay that I'm here for something like that?
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking mirrors, trying to cover the area, or seeking reassurance, to help with how you feel about that part of your face or neck?

Well... um, I guess I do a little bit of that. I hope that's okay to admit. I just like to make sure I look neat and professional for my clients, you know? But... before I leave for work in the mornings, or if I have a meeting, I do find myself going back to the bathroom mirror a few times. Just to adjust my collar, or maybe pull my hair forward a little around my neck so it doesn't stand out so much. And I might... well, sometimes I take another quick look in my phone camera just to be absolutely sure it looks alright. 

I feel a little embarrassed saying this, but I also ask my daughter if it looks strange before I head out. I try not to bother her too much with it, I really do, but I just feel like I need to hear it from someone else. It... well, doing all of that has actually made me late for work more than once, which I feel just awful about because I always try to be reliable. 

Is... is that the sort of thing you meant, doctor? I hope I'm answering your questions right.

Does this concern about how your jaw and neck look cause you a lot of distress, or make it hard for you to do things you normally would, like going to work on time or feeling comfortable in social situations?

Well, um... I guess it does bother me a bit more than I'd like to admit. I really try not to let it get in the way of things, but... well, I have been a little behind on my paperwork lately. It's just that I get so caught up trying to make sure I look presentable before I can focus, and the time just slips away. I feel terrible about it, because I know my supervisor relies on me. 

And, um... I've actually sort of stepped back from taking on any extra responsibilities at work. They offered me a chance to help lead some meetings and do a little supervising, which was so sweet of them, but... I just couldn't do it. The thought of standing up there with everyone looking right at my face and my neck... it just made me too anxious. I told them I was just too busy right now, I hope that was the right thing to say.

I've also... well, I've missed a few of my book club meetings and my walking group lately. It just feels like such a big chore to get ready and make sure everything looks okay before I go out, so sometimes I just stay home instead. I know I shouldn't be so silly about it. Does that make sense, doctor? I hope I'm not sounding too dramatic.
Doctor: Do you find yourself thinking about how your jaw and neck look for most of the day, even when you're trying to focus on other things?

Oh... well, I don't think so. I really try my best not to let it take over, you know? I mean... I wouldn't say it's most of the day. I'm usually so busy with my clients and making sure they're comfortable, I really do try to just put it out of my mind once I finally get to work. 

It might... well, it might pop into my head here and there, especially if I catch my reflection in a window or something, but I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around dwelling on it every single minute. That would be terrible of me. I try very hard to stay focused on the people who need me. 

Is... is that a good thing? I just don't want to give you the wrong impression about how I spend my time.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms align more specifically with F45.22 (Body Dysmorphic Disorder), given the persistent preoccupation with a perceived defect in appearance (jaw and neck), repetitive behaviors (mirror checking, reassurance seeking), and significant impairment in functioning (difficulty taking on responsibilities, social withdrawal). F32.9 (Major Depressive Disorder, unspecified) is less likely as the primary concern due to absence of persistent low mood as the core feature. F44.9 (Dissociative disorder, unspecified) is not supported by the clinical picture.

F44.9 Dissociative disorder not otherwise specified
